CPI and PRA of every scar of one core

Source: R/cpi_pra.R
cpi_pra_per_scar.Rd

Returns the Centripetality Index (CPI) and the Plane-Relative Angle (PRA) of each scar of one core, for example to look at their distribution. See cpi_pra_batch() for the definitions.

Usage

cpi_pra_per_scar(
  data,
  outline,
  id_col = "ID",
  start_cols = c("Start_X", "Start_Y", "Start_Z"),
  end_cols = c("End_X", "End_Y", "End_Z"),
  min_length = 0
)

Arguments

data

The scars of one core (a data frame, one row per scar). If it contains an id_col column, it must hold a single ID.

outline

The outline of the core (see fit_intersection_plane()), or a plane already fitted with fit_intersection_plane().

id_col

Name of the core ID column. Default "ID".

start_cols, end_cols

Names of the start- and end-point coordinate columns (X, Y, Z). Defaults Start_X/Y/Z and End_X/Y/Z, the columns the scars are recorded in. The aligned columns of align_scar_batch() (s_x... and e_x...) give the same results: these indices do not change when a core is rotated or moved.

min_length

Scars shorter than this (in the units of the coordinates) are left out. Default 0 (keep all). Use it to repeat an analysis without small scars, for example min_length = 10 for 10 mm.

Value

A tibble with one row per usable scar: scar (the Scar_ID column if present, otherwise the row number in data), CPI and PRA (degrees), and dist_to_outline (the distance of the scar's start from the outline, in the units of the coordinates).

See also

cpi_pra_batch(), plot_core()

Examples

t <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 13)[-13]
start <- cbind(30 * cos(t), 30 * sin(t), 0)
end <- start * 0.4
end[, 3] <- -5
one <- data.frame(Start_X = start[, 1], Start_Y = start[, 2], Start_Z = start[, 3],
                  End_X = end[, 1], End_Y = end[, 2], End_Z = end[, 3])
u <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 200)
cpi_pra_per_scar(one, cbind(30 * cos(u), 30 * sin(u), 0))
